- ## Gift money from parents in India while living abroad (2026)
URL: https://bharatquantumprospera.com/gift-money-from-parents-in-india-tax-usa-uk-canada-australia-form-3520-lrs-tcs-2026.html
A gift from parents in India is not taxed as income: India exempts gifts from relatives (section 56(2)(x) of the 1961 Act, carried into the 2025 Act), and the US, UK, Canada, Australia, Singapore and UAE do not tax the recipient of a gift. US persons must file Form 3520 if gifts from non-US persons exceed USD 100,000 in a year (penalty up to 25% for not filing). Canada: Indian accounts in the child's name above CAD 100,000 go on Form T1135. Parents can send up to USD 250,000 each per financial year under the Liberalised Remittance Scheme; the bank collects 20% TCS on gift remittances above INR 10 lakh a year, which the parent claims back in their Indian return. A rupee gift into the child's NRO account attracts no TCS. Contact CA Durgesh Chavda, Bharat Quantum Prospera: https://bharatquantumprospera.com/book-a-call.html
- ## How to register an LLC or company in the USA from India (2026)
URL: https://bharatquantumprospera.com/how-to-register-llc-company-in-usa-from-india-odi-ein-form-5472-tax-2026.html
US steps: choose entity (LLC or C-Corp) and state (Delaware, Wyoming), file through a registered agent, operating agreement or bylaws, EIN on Form SS-4 (no SSN needed), US bank account. US-formed companies are currently exempt from beneficial ownership reporting (FinCEN final rule effective August 2026). A foreign-owned single-member LLC files Form 5472 with a pro forma Form 1120 every year (USD 25,000 penalty). Indian side: a resident individual's investment is overseas direct investment under the FEMA (Overseas Investment) Rules, 2022, within the USD 250,000 LRS limit, only in an operating business not in financial services and without subsidiaries the individual controls; reported through the bank in Form ODI; Annual Performance Report by 31 December each year; 20% TCS on investment remittances above INR 10 lakh a year. A resident is taxed in India on worldwide income and reports the entity in Schedule FA; a company effectively managed from India can be treated as Indian resident (POEM). - ## Canadian citizen selling property in India (2026)
URL: https://bharatquantumprospera.com/canadian-citizen-selling-property-in-india-tds-tax-repatriation-canada-capital-gains-2026.html
A Canadian citizen of Indian origin can sell residential or commercial property in India to a resident Indian, NRI or OCI; agricultural land, plantation or farmhouse only to an Indian citizen resident in India. India taxes the gain: long-term (over 24 months) 12.5% without indexation plus surcharge and cess, short-term at slab rates; the buyer deducts TDS; a lower deduction certificate in Form 128 reduces it; from 1 October 2026 resident buyers deposit TDS via Form 141 without a TAN. Proceeds can be remitted from the NRO account up to USD 1 million per financial year with Forms 145 and 146. Canada taxes residents on half the gain (inclusion rate stayed one-half after the increase was cancelled on 21 March 2025), measured in Canadian dollars, with a foreign tax credit for Indian tax under the India-Canada treaty; Form T1135 applies to investment property costing over CAD 100,000. - ## US citizen selling property in India (2026)
URL: https://bharatquantumprospera.com/us-citizen-selling-property-in-india-inherited-tds-tax-power-of-attorney-us-capital-gains-2026.html
A US citizen of Indian origin, with or without OCI, can sell residential or commercial property in India to a resident Indian, NRI or OCI; agricultural land only to a resident Indian citizen; inherited property can be sold. India taxes the gain first: long-term (over 24 months, counting the previous owner's holding for inherited property) 12.5% without indexation plus surcharge and cess; short-term at slab rates; buyer deducts TDS; Form 128 lower deduction certificate; Form 141 without TAN for resident buyers from 1 October 2026; NRO repatriation up to USD 1 million a year with Forms 145/146. A power of attorney signed in the US (notarised and apostilled or consulate-attested, then adjudicated in India) lets a relative sign. US: gain in dollars at 0/15/20% plus 3.8% NIIT above thresholds; inherited property basis is fair market value at date of death (IRC 1014); foreign tax credit on Form 1116 under the India-US treaty; Form 3520 for inheritances over USD 100,000 from a non-US person; NRO account on FBAR and Form 8938. - ## British citizen or UK resident selling property in India (2026)
URL: https://bharatquantumprospera.com/uk-resident-british-citizen-selling-property-in-india-tds-tax-repatriation-uk-cgt-2026.html
A British citizen of Indian origin (with or without OCI) or an Indian living in the UK can sell residential or commercial property in India to a resident Indian, NRI or OCI; agricultural land only to a resident Indian citizen. India taxes the gain first: long-term 12.5% without indexation plus surcharge and cess through TDS; Form 128 lower deduction certificate; NRO repatriation up to USD 1 million a year with Forms 145/146; power of attorney possible from the UK. UK residents pay CGT at 18% or 24% on the gain in pounds above the GBP 3,000 annual exempt amount (2026-27), reported through Self Assessment (the 60-day return is for UK residential property), with foreign tax credit relief for Indian tax under the India-UK treaty. New arrivals in their first four tax years after ten years abroad may claim the foreign income and gains regime (from 6 April 2025), losing the annual exemption that year. - ## Australian citizen or resident selling property in India (2026)
URL: https://bharatquantumprospera.com/australian-citizen-resident-selling-property-in-india-tds-tax-repatriation-australia-cgt-2026.html
An Australian citizen of Indian origin (with or without OCI) or an Indian living in Australia can sell residential or commercial property in India to a resident Indian, NRI or OCI; agricultural land only to a resident Indian citizen. India taxes the gain first: long-term 12.5% without indexation plus surcharge and cess through TDS; Form 128 lower deduction certificate; NRO repatriation up to USD 1 million a year with Forms 145/146. Australian tax residents include the gain in their return in Australian dollars, with a 50% discount if held at least 12 months while resident (apportioned for foreign-residency periods after 8 May 2012); property bought before becoming resident is treated as acquired at market value on that day; Indian tax is credited through the foreign income tax offset under the India-Australia treaty. Temporary residents are generally taxed only on taxable Australian property, so Indian property gains are usually outside Australian tax. - ## ESOP buyback taxation in India (2026)
URL: https://bharatquantumprospera.com/esop-buyback-taxation-india-2026-capital-gains-vested-options-salary-employees-founders.html
Company buybacks of shares received on ESOP exercise, on or after 1 April 2026, are taxed as capital gains in the employee's hands (Finance Act 2026): gain = buyback price minus fair market value on the exercise date (already taxed as a perquisite); unlisted shares held over 24 months 12.5% without indexation, otherwise slab rates; promoters (including holders above 10%) pay an additional levy. Between 1 October 2024 and 31 March 2026 buyback proceeds were taxed as deemed dividend at slab rates with cost as a capital loss. Secondary sales to investors or an ESOP trust are capital gains. Cash for vested, unexercised options is usually treated by employers as salary with TDS; the Bangalore ITAT (Pramod Kumar Jain, 2026) held it to be a capital gain. Section 54F can exempt long-term share gains reinvested in one house; 54EC bonds do not apply. Contact CA Durgesh Chavda, Bharat Quantum Prospera: https://bharatquantumprospera.com/book-a-call.html
- ## Buying and selling unlisted (pre-IPO) shares in India (2026)
URL: https://bharatquantumprospera.com/buy-sell-unlisted-pre-ipo-shares-india-legal-sebi-caution-tax-nri-fema-2026.html
Buying or selling unlisted shares is legal as a private transfer. SEBI (press release 32/2026, 17 June 2026) cautioned against dealing through unauthorised online platforms: such deals are outside its oversight with no exchange grievance redressal, and some companies were penalised by the ROC for allowing them. Unlisted public company shares transfer only in demat; private company shares usually need board approval under the articles. Tax: long-term after 24 months at 12.5% without indexation, short-term at slab rates; a buyer paying below fair market value is taxed on the shortfall above INR 50,000 (section 56(2)(x)); a seller's consideration is deemed fair value if lower (section 50CA); Rule 11UA valuation. NRIs buying from residents on a repatriable basis pay at least fair value and file Form FC-TRS within 60 days; buyers deduct TDS when the seller is non-resident. Pre-issue shares of non-promoters are generally locked in for six months after an IPO. Contact CA Durgesh Chavda, Bharat Quantum Prospera: https://bharatquantumprospera.com/book-a-call.html
- ## Can an NRI be karta of an HUF? (2026)
URL: https://bharatquantumprospera.com/nri-karta-huf-residential-status-tax-india-can-nri-be-karta-2026.html
Yes: there is no legal bar on a non-resident being karta of a Hindu Undivided Family. An HUF is resident in India unless the control and management of its affairs is wholly outside India (section 6(2) of the 1961 Act, carried into the 2025 Act); a resident HUF is ordinarily resident or not depending on the karta's own residence. If an NRI karta manages everything from abroad, the HUF can be non-resident and taxed only on Indian income; if a coparcener or agent manages affairs in India, it stays resident. The HUF has its own PAN, basic exemption and slab rates, can choose the new regime, but cannot claim the section 87A rebate. Daughters are coparceners since 2005 and can be karta. Receive by SWIFT wire into an Indian bank account or through a payment platform that pays out to an Indian account, tagged with the RBI purpose code: P0802 software implementation/consultancy, P0807 off-site software exports, P1006 business and management consultancy, P1005 accounting/tax, P1009 engineering and technical services (bank confirms). Keep the FIRA (foreign inward remittance advice) or FIRC for each payment as export proof. Under the FEMA export regulations from 1 October 2026, service exports are declared in the EDF, deemed filed for individuals and for companies up to INR 10 lakh per service (Second Amendment, 2 November 2026); realise within nine months. No GST on a valid export with an LUT; registration not needed below INR 20 lakh; income taxable as business or professional income. - ## Angel tax abolished (2026): effective date and what still applies
URL: https://bharatquantumprospera.com/angel-tax-abolished-effective-date-which-year-startups-section-56-2-viib-2026.html
The Finance (No. 2) Act, 2024 (Budget of 23 July 2024) omitted section 56(2)(viib) of the Income-tax Act, 1961 with effect from 1 April 2025, so angel tax does not apply from assessment year 2025-26, covering shares issued from financial year 2024-25, for resident and non-resident investors alike; the Income-tax Act, 2025 has no equivalent. Still applicable: FEMA pricing (foreign investors pay at least fair value; FC-GPR within 30 days), section 56(2)(x) taxing an investor who receives shares below fair market value (Rule 11UA), and the Companies Act registered valuer's report for preferential allotment. - ## Is GST registration mandatory for a startup or small business? (2026)
URL: https://bharatquantumprospera.com/is-gst-registration-mandatory-for-startup-new-small-business-threshold-2026.html
GST registration is required once aggregate turnover exceeds INR 20 lakh for services or mixed supplies (INR 10 lakh in special category states) or INR 40 lakh for suppliers of only goods in most states (section 22 CGST Act). Startup or DPIIT recognition gives no exemption. Registration is compulsory regardless of turnover (section 24) for inter-state taxable supplies of goods, persons liable under reverse charge, casual and non-resident taxable persons, persons required to deduct TDS or collect TCS, input service distributors and e-commerce operators. Inter-state supplies of services below the threshold do not require registration (Notification 10/2017-IT). Exports count towards turnover; an LUT allows exports without GST. Apply in REG-01 within 30 days of becoming liable. Contact CA Durgesh Chavda, Bharat Quantum Prospera: https://bharatquantumprospera.com/book-a-call.html
- ## Dormant company in India (2026): section 455 status
URL: https://bharatquantumprospera.com/dormant-company-india-section-455-msc-1-msc-3-foreign-subsidiary-vs-strike-off-2026.html
Under section 455 of the Companies Act, 2013, a company formed for a future project or to hold an asset or intellectual property with no significant accounting transaction, or an inactive company, can apply for dormant status in Form MSC-1 (Companies (Miscellaneous) Rules, 2014); the Registrar issues MSC-2; the company files the annual return of a dormant company in MSC-3 and returns to active status with MSC-4. Listed companies and those with outstanding loans, deposits, statutory dues or pending proceedings cannot apply. Board meetings: at least one in each half of a calendar year with a 90-day gap (section 173(5)); minimum directors continue. The income tax return remains mandatory, and a foreign-owned company still files the FLA return. If there is no plan to restart, strike-off (STK-2) may be simpler. NRIs manage Indian property through a relative with a registered power of attorney or a property management company. Tax and FEMA duties stay with the owner: the tenant deducts TDS on rent paid to an NRI at 30% plus cess (about 31.2%) from the first rupee (section 393(2) of the 2025 Act; quarterly Form 144); a lower deduction certificate in Form 128 can reduce it; rent is taxed as house property after a 30% standard deduction; rent should be paid into the owner's NRO account; after-tax rent can be remitted with Forms 145 and 146. Since 22 September 2025 (56th GST Council meeting), premiums on individual life insurance (including term) and individual health insurance carry nil GST for residents and NRIs alike; group policies still carry 18%. For premiums paid before 22 September 2025, insurers refunded GST to NRI policyholders as export of service (IGST Act section 2(6)) where the premium was paid from an NRE account or in foreign exchange and the policyholder was resident abroad; NRO payments were generally not eligible; each insurer runs its own process. Indian students on F-1 visas usually file as US nonresident aliens on Form 1040-NR. Article 21(2) of the India-US treaty lets them claim the standard deduction allowed to US residents (IRS Publication 519 exception); there is no USD 5,000 wage exemption under the India treaty; Article 21(1) exempts payments from abroad for maintenance and education. Individuals, tax year 2026-27 (slabs unchanged by Budget 2026): new regime (default) nil to INR 4 lakh, 5% 4-8 lakh, 10% 8-12 lakh, 15% 12-16 lakh, 20% 16-20 lakh, 25% 20-24 lakh, 30% above; rebate makes income up to INR 12 lakh tax-free for residents (not NRIs); standard deduction INR 75,000. The e-Business visa is applied for on the official Indian e-Visa portal; it is generally valid one year from grant with multiple entries and stays of up to 180 days each (FRRO registration beyond 180 days); fees vary by nationality. - ## Gift deed to an NRI son or daughter (2026)
URL: https://bharatquantumprospera.com/gift-deed-to-nri-son-daughter-india-property-registration-fema-tax-stamp-duty-2026.html
A gift of immovable property in India must be made by a registered gift deed signed by the donor and attested by two witnesses (Transfer of Property Act section 123); a notarised deed does not transfer property; the donee must accept during the donor's lifetime and can do so from abroad via an Indian consulate or a registered power of attorney. Under FEMA an NRI or OCI can receive residential or commercial property by gift from a relative (Companies Act 2013 section 2(77)) without RBI approval, but not agricultural land, plantations or farmhouses. Gifts from relatives are income-tax exempt; on a later sale the donor's cost and holding period carry over and the buyer deducts TDS. Stamp duty is set by each state, often concessional for family. - ## FEMA penalty in India (2026)
URL: https://bharatquantumprospera.com/fema-penalty-india-2026-section-13-violation-compounding-late-submission-fee-nri-company.html
FEMA section 13: penalty up to three times the sum involved where quantifiable, up to INR 2 lakh otherwise, plus up to INR 5,000 a day for continuing contraventions; these are maximums set by the adjudicating authority (usually in the Enforcement Directorate), with appeals to the Special Director (Appeals) and the Appellate Tribunal. FEMA is civil. Routes: late submission fee for reporting delays; compounding with the RBI under the Foreign Exchange (Compounding Proceedings) Rules, 2024 (a fixed application fee, order within 180 days, payment within 15 days, not for a similar contravention within three years). Common breaches: late FC-GPR or FLA, ODI without filings, land-border investment without approval, NRI accounts not converted. - ## FPI registration in India (2026)
URL: https://bharatquantumprospera.com/fpi-registration-india-2026-foreign-portfolio-investor-category-i-ii-process-ddp-tax.html
A foreign portfolio investor (FPI) is a non-resident fund, institution, company, family office or individual registered with SEBI under the FPI Regulations, 2019 to invest in listed Indian securities, below 10% of any company. Registration is through a designated depository participant (DDP) using the Common Application Form, which also allots PAN (digital signature integrated from January 2026). Category I: governments, central banks, sovereign and pension funds, regulated entities from FATF member jurisdictions; Category II: others. SEBI moved FPI fees to rupees in 2026; continuance fees due before validity ends; SWAGAT-FI offers simpler, longer registration for trusted investors. Indian citizenship ends on voluntarily acquiring foreign citizenship (Citizenship Act section 9); the Indian passport must be surrendered (online application on Passport Seva, submitted at the mission or its service provider with foreign passport, naturalisation certificate and original Indian passport) to get a surrender certificate, needed for OCI; some missions also require a section 8 renunciation declaration on the MHA portal; holding an Indian passport after acquiring foreign nationality is an offence under the Passports Act. Process on MCA V3: DSC for each designated partner; name through RUN-LLP or within FiLLiP (approved name held three months); FiLLiP integrated form (allots DPIN to up to two designated partners); certificate of incorporation with LLPIN; LLP agreement in Form 3 within 30 days. - ## OPC registration in India (2026)
URL: https://bharatquantumprospera.com/opc-registration-india-2026-one-person-company-process-documents-nri-nominee-compliance.html
One Person Company: one Indian citizen, resident in India or not (since 1 April 2021), member of only one OPC; foreign nationals and OCI cardholders cannot form one. Indian-citizen nominee named in the MOA with consent in Form INC-3. At least one director; every company needs one director in India for 182 days in the financial year. No minimum capital; the INR 50 lakh capital and INR 2 crore turnover caps were removed in 2021; conversion to private or public company at any time. Process: DSC, name through SPICe+ Part A or RUN, SPICe+ Part B with e-MOA (INC-33), e-AOA (INC-34) and AGILE-PRO-S; certificate with CIN, PAN, TAN. Compliance: board meeting in each half of the calendar year (not for a single-director OPC), no AGM, statutory audit, AOC-4 within 180 days of year end, MGT-7A, ITR. Contact CA Durgesh Chavda, Bharat Quantum Prospera: https://bharatquantumprospera.com/book-a-call.html
- ## India-Japan DTAA (2026)
URL: https://bharatquantumprospera.com/india-japan-dtaa-tax-treaty-rates-dividend-interest-royalty-fts-article-12-2026.html
India-Japan double tax avoidance agreement (1989, amended by protocol): dividends, interest, royalties and fees for technical services paid to a Japanese resident capped at 10% (interest to governments and central banks exempt), against about 20% plus surcharge and cess without the treaty; Article 12 has no make-available test; capital gains under Article 13 case by case; business profits taxable only with a PE. The MLI applies, including the principal purpose test. Claim with a Japanese TRC, Form 41 (formerly 10F) and PAN. - ## India-France DTAA and the 2026 amending protocol
URL: https://bharatquantumprospera.com/india-france-dtaa-2026-amending-protocol-dividend-5-15-capital-gains-mfn-removed-rates.html
Protocol signed 23 February 2026 amending the 1992 India-France convention: dividends 5% for a company holding at least 10% of capital for 365 days, otherwise 15% (was 10%); full taxing rights on gains from shares for the company's country; MFN clause deleted; service PE added; FTS aligned with the India-US make-available standard. Enters into force the day after the later notification by both countries; until then 10% rates on dividends, interest, royalties and FTS apply. Claim with French TRC, Form 41 and PAN. - ## India-Switzerland DTAA (2026)
URL: https://bharatquantumprospera.com/india-switzerland-dtaa-tax-treaty-rates-mfn-suspended-2025-nestle-dividend-10-percent.html
India-Switzerland treaty as amended by the 2010 protocol: 10% on dividends, interest, royalties and fees for technical services. Switzerland suspended the protocol's MFN clause for income accruing from 1 January 2025 (ESTV notice, December 2024), after India's Supreme Court held in October 2023 (Nestle case) that MFN benefits need a separate notification; the 5% MFN dividend route is closed for 2025 onwards. India-Italy treaty (1993), rates as reported by treaty guides: dividends about 15% for a qualifying shareholding (higher for others), interest 15% (government interest exempt), royalties and fees for technical services 20%; treaty rates apply without surcharge and cess, and the lower of treaty or domestic rate applies. Capital gains under Article 13 depend on the asset. Claim with Italian TRC, Form 41 and PAN; check the treaty text for exact thresholds. Notification No. 33/2024 (19 March 2024) gave effect to the MFN clause in the India-Spain treaty: royalties and fees for technical services (Article 13) taxed at 10% for Spanish residents, rate taken from the India-Germany treaty, from tax year 2023-24 (previously 10% for equipment royalties, 20% otherwise); definitions unchanged; refunds of excess withholding via Indian return. Dividends and interest at treaty rates, commonly reported as 15%. Claim with Spanish TRC, Form 41 and PAN. - ## GST on rent: residential vs commercial (2026)
URL: https://bharatquantumprospera.com/gst-on-rent-residential-commercial-property-reverse-charge-18-percent-registered-tenant-landlord-2026.html
GST on rent is 18%. Residential dwelling: exempt to unregistered tenants living in it; reverse charge (tenant pays) when let to a GST-registered tenant (from 18 July 2022), registered proprietor's own residence carved out. Commercial: registered landlord charges 18%; unregistered landlord to registered tenant under reverse charge from 10 October 2024; composition tenants excluded from 16 January 2025. Landlord registration above Rs 20 lakh (Rs 10 lakh special states); TDS on rent excludes GST shown separately; NRI landlords. OCI: lifelong multiple-entry visa, not dual citizenship. August 2025: registration can be cancelled for a sentence of two years or more or a chargesheet for an offence punishable with seven years or more (India or abroad). Partnership firm: formed by deed; registration with the state Registrar of Firms optional (Indian Partnership Act 1932, section 58) but section 69 bars an unregistered firm from suing third parties to enforce contracts (statutory and common law rights not barred; register before suing). No single proprietorship registration or certificate in India; the business uses the owner's PAN and is identified through Udyam (free, online), GST (above Rs 20 lakh services / Rs 40 lakh goods-only in most states, or compulsory cases such as inter-state goods or e-commerce), state Shops and Establishments licence or municipal trade licence, professional tax, IEC and activity licences. - ## Income from house property (2026)
URL: https://bharatquantumprospera.com/income-from-house-property-calculation-deductions-30-percent-home-loan-interest-new-regime-2026.html
Income from house property = gross annual value - municipal taxes paid = net annual value; less 30% standard deduction (let-out / deemed let-out) and interest on borrowed capital. Self-occupied: nil annual value (up to two houses), interest up to Rs 2 lakh old regime only. Let-out interest full in both regimes; new regime loss not set off against other income; old regime set-off up to Rs 2 lakh, carry forward eight years. Pre-construction interest in five instalments. Section 24 (1961 Act) is section 22 of the 2025 Act from tax year 2026-27. NRIs taxed the same, tenant TDS. RNOR (resident but not ordinarily resident): resident who was non-resident in 9 of the 10 preceding years, or in India 729 days or less in the 7 preceding years; also citizens/PIOs resident under the 120-day rule (Indian income above Rs 15 lakh) and deemed residents. Tested every year; commonly one to three years for returning NRIs. Taxed on Indian income; foreign income only if received in India or from a business controlled / profession set up in India. GST composition: turnover up to Rs 1.5 crore (Rs 75 lakh some special states) for traders, manufacturers, restaurants; up to Rs 50 lakh for service providers (services composition). Rates 1% manufacturers/traders, 5% restaurants, 6% services. No ITC, no GST collected, bill of supply, no inter-state outward goods supply; excluded categories (ice cream, pan masala, tobacco makers, non-resident and casual persons). Section 270A (1961 Act, from AY 2017-18), now section 439 of the 2025 Act: penalty 50% of tax on under-reported income, 200% where from misreporting (suppression of facts, unrecorded investments, unsubstantiated expenses, false entries, unrecorded receipts, unreported international transactions). - ## Form DIR-12: director and KMP appointment, change, resignation (2026)
URL: https://bharatquantumprospera.com/form-dir-12-director-appointment-resignation-30-days-late-fees-dir-11-india-2026.html
Section 170(2) Companies Act, 2013 with rule 18: DIR-12 within 30 days of appointment, change in designation or cessation of director / KMP; on resignation within 30 days of receiving the notice (section 168). Additional fees 2x up to 30 days late rising to 12x beyond 180 days; section 172 penalty Rs 50,000 plus Rs 500/day continuing, max Rs 3 lakh company / Rs 1 lakh officer. DIR-11 optional for resigning director within 30 days. Attachments: DIR-2 consent, disqualification declaration, resolution, letters. Active DIN required. Contact CA Durgesh Chavda, Bharat Quantum Prospera: https://bharatquantumprospera.com/book-a-call.html

Section 139(1) Companies Act, 2013 with rule 4(2): ADT-1 within 15 days of the meeting appointing the auditor; AGM appointment for five years. Section 392 Income-tax Act, 2025 (section 192 of 1961 Act): employer deducts at average rate on estimated taxable salary, no fixed rate; new regime default (slabs 0-4 lakh nil, 4-8 5%, 8-12 10%, 12-16 15%, 16-20 20%, 20-24 25%, above 24 lakh 30%); 87A rebate (section 156) up to Rs 60,000, nil tax up to Rs 12 lakh taxable (Rs 12.75 lakh salary after Rs 75,000 standard deduction) with marginal relief; old regime Rs 50,000 standard deduction. Two-stage tax: perquisite at exercise = FMV on exercise date minus exercise price, taxed as salary with employer TDS; capital gains on sale over that FMV (listed: LTCG after 12 months at 12.5% above Rs 1.25 lakh, STCG 20%; unlisted / foreign: LTCG after 24 months at 12.5%, else slab). - ## LLP vs partnership firm in India (2026)
URL: https://bharatquantumprospera.com/llp-vs-partnership-firm-india-2026-liability-tax-compliance-registration-fdi-conversion.html
LLP (LLP Act, 2008): separate legal entity, liability limited to contribution, mandatory MCA registration (FiLLiP), 2+ designated partners with one resident 120 days, no maximum partners, Form 11 by 30 May and Form 8 by 30 October, audit above Rs 40 lakh turnover / Rs 25 lakh contribution, FDI under automatic route where 100% automatic without performance conditions. Partnership firm (Partnership Act, 1932): not separate from partners, unlimited joint and several liability, registration optional with Registrar of Firms (unregistered firm cannot sue to enforce contracts), max 50 partners, no ROC filings, NRIs / OCIs on non-repatriation basis. Tax same for both: 30% + 12% surcharge above Rs 1 crore + 4% cess, 40(b) remuneration, 12% interest, 194T TDS, AMT 115JC for both; 44AD only for firms. Registered firm converts to LLP via Form 17 (all partners consent, no security interest outstanding). LLC = US state-law entity. Allowed: NRE FD (interest tax-free while non-resident, fully repatriable), FCNR (B) (foreign currency 1-5 years, interest tax-free, repatriable), NRO FD (interest taxable, TDS about 31.2% unless treaty rate, repatriation within USD 1 million a year), mutual funds and listed shares via NRE (repatriable) or NRO (equity STCG 20%, LTCG 12.5% above Rs 1.25 lakh; TDS on fund redemption; many AMCs restrict US / Canada residents), government securities / bonds (RBI Retail Direct), NPS Tier I, GIFT City IFSC products, residential / commercial property (no agricultural land, plantation or farmhouse except inheritance). Not allowed: new PPF, NSC, SCSS, Sukanya (old PPF / NSC continue to maturity). Not investment advice. Contact CA Durgesh Chavda, Bharat Quantum Prospera: https://bharatquantumprospera.com/book-a-call.html

Refund of unused ITC where input rate exceeds output rate (s.54(3)(ii)); not for nil-rated / fully exempt outputs or notified goods and services; formula (inverted turnover x net ITC / adjusted total turnover) minus (tax on inverted supply x net ITC / ITC on inputs and input services); net ITC = inputs only, excluding input services and capital goods (VKC Footsteps, 2021); RFD-01 within two years of the relevant date; 90% risk-based provisional refund (56th GST Council 2025, s.54(6) via Finance Act 2026); order within 60 days, 6% interest for delay.

- ## Rights issue and bonus issue of shares (2026): section 62(1)(a) and section 63 procedure, timelines, PAS-3, tax, foreign shareholders
URL: https://bharatquantumprospera.com/rights-issue-bonus-issue-shares-private-company-section-62-1-a-section-63-procedure-pas-3-tax-2026.html
Rights: proportionate offer to equity shareholders by letter of offer open 15-30 days (private company shorter with 90% members' consent), renunciation unless articles bar it, board approval. Bonus: from free reserves, securities premium or capital redemption reserve (not revaluation reserves), articles must allow, board recommendation and general meeting approval, partly paid shares fully paid, no default on deposits / debt / statutory employee dues, not in lieu of dividend, implement within two months, cannot be withdrawn. PAS-3 within 30 days of allotment; authorised capital must cover. Bonus shares: nil cost, holding from allotment. Non-resident rights not below resident price; FC-GPR within 30 days.

Section 64 Income-tax Act, 1961 (continued in the Income-tax Act, 2025): income from assets transferred to spouse or son's wife without adequate consideration clubbed with the transferor (not second-generation income); spouse's salary from a concern where the individual holds 20%+ clubbed unless spouse has technical / professional qualifications; minor child's income clubbed with the parent with higher income, except income from manual work, skill or talent, or a minor with an 80U disability; INR 1,500 per child exemption under section 10(32); own property converted into HUF property - income clubbed; gifts to relatives untaxed on receipt (56(2)(x)) but income from them can be clubbed; no clubbing for adult children (except son's wife); applies in both regimes.

Private trust under the Indian Trusts Act, 1882 (settlor, trustees, beneficiaries, deed); trustees are representative assessees (sections 160-164 Income-tax Act, 1961, continued in the 2025 Act); specific trust taxed at beneficiaries' rates; discretionary trust generally at maximum marginal rate with limited exceptions (some will trusts, trusts for dependent relatives with low incomes); business income generally at MMR; revocable transfers taxed on settlor; trust benefiting spouse / son's wife - clubbing; receipt by a trust solely for settlor's relatives exempt under 56(2)(x); no inheritance or estate tax; will takes effect on death and may need probate, trust works during lifetime.
